data.long_meaning: Chhatra means umbrella or fort and Pal means lord. The name Chhatrapal is derived from Sanskrit and means 'Lord of Forts'. In Hindu mythology, Chhatrapal is an epithet of several gods, particularly Lord Shiva and Lord Vishnu. The name Chhatrapal carries the meaning “Lord of Forts” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Chhatrapal usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of forts and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_sanskrit.name: चत्रपल
in_sanskrit.meaning: holder of an umbrella or an umbrella itself
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The name Chhatrapal is derived from the Sanskrit words 'chatra' meaning 'umbrella' or 'parasol', and 'pal' meaning 'holder'. Therefore, Chhatrapal can be translated to mean 'holder of an umbrella' or 'umbrella itself'. In Hindu mythology, the god Indra is often depicted carrying an umbrella, so the name Chhatrapal can also be considered a reference to Indra.
